e7_s4_rationale: The patient's symptoms, including intensively pruritic papules and the histopathology findings of mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, are consistent with Grover disease, a rare skin condition characterized by sudden onset of pruritic papules.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Darier disease
e7_s4_rejected.why: Darier disease typically presents with greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas and has a strong familial component, which is not mentioned in the case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
e7_s4_rejected.why: Pityriasis rubra pilaris is characterized by orange-red scaling plaques and palmoplantar keratoderma, which are not present in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Lichen planus
e7_s4_rejected.why: Lichen planus typically presents with flat-topped, violaceous papules and can involve the mucous membranes, which is not consistent with this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Keratosis punctata
e7_s4_rejected.why: Keratosis punctata is characterized by multiple small, hyperkeratotic papules on the palms, which is not consistent with the distribution of lesions in this case.
